ArtifactHandle.description: A pointer to a bounded, readable artifact.

description.description: What the artifact contains, so a caller can decide whether to read it.

uri.description: Always a `library-evidence://` URI -- enforced by [`ArtifactUri`], not only by the schema.

Coverage.description:
What was actually looked at, and what was not.

`ok` means successful within this scope, never complete knowledge of a library. An empty
`search_evidence` result with `indexed: ["public_api"]` is a valid negative answer; the same
result with `missing: ["public_api"]` is an evidence gap. The two must never collapse.

indexed.description: Evidence kinds that were successfully indexed.

limitations.description: Known reasons this result may not generalize.

missing.description: Evidence kinds that were expected but are absent.

scope.description: What the result claims to cover, in prose.

Error.description:
A typed failure with a concrete next action.

Emitted into `$defs` as `Error`; the Rust name avoids colliding with `std::error::Error` at
every use site. Renaming this type, or dropping the `rename`, leaves a dangling `$ref` in
the root conditionals -- `wire_conformance::every_ref_in_the_schema_resolves` catches that.

code.description: The stable code a caller can branch on.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Not a stable interface.

next_action.description: What the caller should do instead. Blueprint §7.2 requires this, not just a code.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the identical request could succeed.

Evidence.description:
One supporting fact, with the provenance needed to check it.

Blueprint §7.2: every entry carries an ID, class, subject, exact locator, source-version
match and producer, plus a compact excerpt -- not an unexplained numeric confidence.

artifact_id.description: The artifact this was read out of.

evidence_class.description: Which epistemic class this fact belongs to.

locator.description: Position within the artifact. Specialized as a discriminated union per producer.

producer_version.description: The exact producer version, for reproducibility.

source_version_match.description: How the source's version relates to the requested one.

subject.description: What the fact is about -- a symbol path, a setting, a release.

Freshness.description: Registry freshness. Blueprint §3.3: freshness is not one timestamp.

latest_verified.description:
Whether "this is the latest release" was actually revalidated. A cache hit alone is not
evidence that a release is still latest.

registry_checked_at.description: When the registry was last consulted, or `null` if it was not consulted at all.

source_version_match.description: How the evidence's source version relates to the requested one.

JobHandle.description: A receipt for submitted work. Never evidence that the work finished.

job_id.description: Durable core job identity. Distinct from the request ID: jobs are shared and reusable.

poll_after_ms.description: Advisory next-poll delay. Not a completion-time guarantee.

stage.description: Which stage is executing, for a caller to report progress.

Pagination.description:
Bounded-result accounting (blueprint §7.3).

A first page is not the whole result set. A cursor binds the query digest, snapshot, filters
and sort, so a mismatched cursor is rejected with `INVALID_CURSOR` rather than producing an
inconsistent page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

returned.description: How many entries this page carries.

total_matches.description: Total matches when known. `null` means "not counted", never "zero".

truncated.description: Whether output was cut short by a budget.

description:
The response envelope every tool returns.

`status`, `job` and `error` are private: [`Envelope::new`] and the [`Outcome`] enum are the
only way to populate them, which is what makes the cross-field rule a type-level fact rather
than a convention.

coverage.description: What was looked at, and what was not.

status.description:
The four result statuses (blueprint §7.2).

The values are, in order: `ok`, `partial`, `pending`, `error`. `ok` means successful within
the declared coverage, not complete knowledge; `partial` carries usable evidence *and* gaps.

No variant carries a doc comment -- see the module docs in [`super`](crate::wire).

summary.description: One-line account of what this result establishes.
